findings.title: The center column carries no 2-adic structure: agreement density is 0.500 in every v2 bucket
findings.claim: My own wild hypothesis, tested and REFUTED. Round two established that left-edge agreement depth is a function of v2(p) alone (8, 29, 400 at v2=1,2,3), i.e. 2-adically close rows agree deeply. The extrapolation was that the center column inherits this rigidity, pinning any period P to a valuation class. It does not. A(k), the fraction of t with c(t)==c(t+k), bucketed by v2(k) over T=60000 and all k<=512, is 0.500 to three decimals in every bucket from v2=0 to v2=7. The same orbit is dyadically rigid at the left edge and dyadically structureless at the center, so boundary regularity does not transport inward.
findings.scope: Phi(a)=a XOR ((a<<1)|(a<<2)), seed 1; center cell of row t at bit t (verified against the hand picture at t=0 and t=1); T=60000; k=1..512; single seed. Pure enumeration.
findings.result: Ran. Hypothesis refuted on its own pre-stated kill test.

verification.limits: T=60000; k<=512; one seed; no solver; under 5 minutes on one core.

limitations: Finite horizon and k<=512. Absence of a dyadic effect here is not proof of absence.
Tests the center column in the coordinate t only; F003 argues that is the wrong coordinate, so this does not refute interface-indexed variants.
findings.next_action: Treat as a standing filter: any proposal carrying a boundary invariant inward must explain why it evades this.

findings.title: The v2>=4 growth law is exactly 3/4 of t, placing the regular/chaotic interface at velocity -1/4
findings.claim: CORRECTS my round-two response, which reported the regular region as about 0.375 of the cone and stated that I had searched for a clean law and failed. Fitting through the origin gives depth(t,16) = 0.749994 * t over t in [100,12000), i.e. exactly (3/4)t, which is 3/8 of the cone width 2t+1. With the left edge at -t and the regular region reaching (3/4)t inward, the interface sits at -t/4: velocity exactly -1/4 in cone units, one cell per four steps, matching the period-4 ether whose depth I measured at 29.
findings.scope: Same frame and seed; T=12000; t in [100,12000); p in {16,32,64}; least squares through the origin.

verification.limits: T=12000; three periods; no solver; under 5 minutes on one core.

limitations: A six-digit fit at p=16, not a derivation. I have no argument for why the constant is 3/4.
The droop at p=32 and p=64 (0.7485, 0.7455) is unexplained; finite-horizon warm-up is not separated from a real p dependence.
The velocity -1/4 reading assumes the left edge sits at -t in cone units, which is the frame convention, not a measured fact.
findings.next_action: Derive 3/4 from the ether tiling, or refute it at larger T; then check whether the interface is literally a period-4 particle.

findings.title: Wild swing: re-index the center column by distance to the interface rather than by t
findings.claim: Proposal, not run. F002 puts the interface at the rational velocity -1/4, which says it is a period-4 traveling particle rather than a statistical edge. Proposal: stop indexing the center column by t and index it by distance to that interface, m(t) = (5/4)t, or by the period-4 particle phase at the center position. Rationale: F001 tested the center column in t, and t is the coordinate we impose because it is how we run the machine; the dynamics has its own clock. An observable periodic against an internal clock looks like a fair coin against t, which is exactly the shape F001 returned. Pre-stated KILL TEST: compute A_phase(k), center-column agreement bucketed by period-4 interface phase at each endpoint instead of by v2(k). If the buckets sit at 0.500 as in F001, this dies immediately.
findings.scope: Mechanism shape with a pre-stated kill test. Nothing computed.
limitations: F001 is direct evidence that the center column resists this whole family of ideas; this is a bet that the coordinate was wrong, not that F001 was.
Rests on F002, whose 3/4 is a fit rather than a derivation.
No ordinal, no proof obligation discharged, and no claim that structure in the interface coordinate would settle Problem 1 even if found.
May be a rename of existing defect or particle analyses. If the period-4 interface particle is already catalogued, this adds nothing.
findings.next_action: Run the stated kill test before any further investment.
